what: openCH CH32V307: an I2C transfer to an address nobody answers on, and whether the bus survives it
board: openCH CH32V307 (WCH-Link CH549F, OpenOCD wch-riscv.cfg, adapter speed 1000)

probe_image.program: openocd -f wch-riscv.cfg -c 'adapter speed 1000' -c init -c halt -c 'program <elf> verify' -c reset

green.stdout: osal_stall_probe_ok stage=15 loops=3 wait=0x80000000 get=0xfffffffe uart=7/7 i2c=4/4 nak=0xfffffffa recover=0x68 recv_ms=10 ticks=0x11ce->0x1bda

red.what_changed: one temporary local edit, never committed: the 'unanswered' read was pointed at 0x68 (the address that does answer)
red.expected: the wired judgement must reject a transfer that comes back as success
red.stdout:
osal_stall_probe failed:
- an unanswered I2C address returned 0, expected 0xfffffffa (XY_HAL_ERROR_NOT_FOUND)
red.restore: source copied back from a byte-exact backup, sha256 re-checked (92a0d47f...), rebuilt ELF reproduced 5aa034f9... bit-for-bit, reflashed, same validator green again

boundaries: One board, one image, one run per state. The NAK is an address-NACK from an absent address, not clock stretching, a busy slave, a held-low bus, or arbitration loss.
It does not cover the I2C timeout path, repeated-start failures, or recovery after a bus that is already broken when the probe starts.
uart 7/7 and ticks 0x11ce->0x1bda are liveness readings from the same run, not a stability claim.
The RED came from a manual temporary edit and will not re-run automatically; only the contract tests and the probe guard are permanent.
